title: Deltoris: Enabling Real-time VLA Inference in Embodied AI via Bit-level Sparsity and Speculative Inference
event_hint: Deltoris: an algorithm-hardware co-design framework accelerating diffusion-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) inference for embodied AI using temporal-aware bit-sparsity, speculative inference, and a 1D systolic bit-serial PE array accelerator.
problem: Diffusion-based VLA models produce smooth motion and good generalization for robot control but are compute-intensive and must run at high control frequency (50-200 Hz), imposing strict latency/energy constraints on edge devices. Existing robotic platforms miss real-time targets: the PAD VLA model runs at only 2.0 Hz on a mobile Nvidia Orin SoC.
mechanism: Deltoris exploits high temporal similarity in robotic control loops (over 98% of pixels between consecutive camera frames are often unchanged). (1) A temporal-aware bit-sparsity algorithm computes only the differences between consecutive inputs, representing differential inputs in binary and executing only active '1' bits (up to 92.9% operation reduction). (2) A speculative inference technique (inspired by LLM speculative decoding) lets a lightweight VLA model predict multiple future actions that a heavier VLA model validates, amortizing weight/intermediate data loading across validation steps to cut the extra off-chip traffic that naive bit-sparsity would add (1.8x traffic increase). (3) A dedicated accelerator with customized 1D systolic bit-serial PE arrays and an output-stationary dataflow eliminates PE workload imbalance seen in prior bit-serial accelerators.

evidence.claim: Deltoris achieves up to 34.2x speedup over mobile GPUs and up to 6.1x over prior accelerators, while maintaining comparable accuracy.
evidence.condition: abstract headline; detailed baseline breakdown in results

evidence.claim: The PAD VLA model executes at only 2.0 Hz on a mobile Nvidia Orin SoC, far below the 50-200 Hz real-time requirement, motivating the work.
evidence.condition: PAD model on Nvidia Jetson Orin SoC

evidence.claim: Over 98% of pixels between consecutive camera frames often remain unchanged due to the small inter-control interval; the temporal-aware bit-sparsity algorithm achieves up to 92.9% operation reduction.
evidence.value: >98% pixels unchanged; up to 92.9% op reduction
evidence.condition: consecutive frames in robotic control loop

evidence.claim: A naive bit-sparsity implementation increases off-chip data traffic by 1.8x, shifting workloads from compute-bound to memory-bound; the proposed speculative inference technique amortizes data loading across validation steps to mitigate this.

Hardware comparison: Deltoris (128 rows of PE array x 64 PEs, 2.45 mm^2 at 16nm) is compared against GPU (mobile Ampere in Nvidia Orin), Pragmatic, BBS, Cambricon-D, Exion and Ditto; a speculative window size of 3 is reported as the best speedup/accuracy tradeoff.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 10 - Table 2; PDF Page 12

evaluation_context: Algorithm-hardware co-design evaluated against six hardware baselines (mobile Ampere GPU in Nvidia Jetson Orin SoC, Pragmatic, BBS, Cambricon-D, Exion, Ditto) with area reported at 16nm; default accelerator config 128 PE arrays x 64 PEs (2.45 mm^2). Accuracy evaluated on UVA-P (PushT) and UVA-L (LIBERO) datasets. Sensitivity studies cover PE array size, on-chip buffer size and speculation threshold. No end-to-end robot-task success-rate-vs-latency on physical hardware is in the visible evidence.
limitations: Visible evidence focuses on algorithmic mechanism, hardware design, and speedup/energy sensitivity; the detailed end-to-end speedup breakdown by baseline and the absolute Hz achieved on the target platform are in results sections not fully exposed. Real-robot deployment latency (vs simulation/emulation) and power consumption in watts are not shown in the visible evidence. Accuracy is described as 'comparable' (negligible loss on UVA-P/UVA-L); a rapid-motion scenario accuracy figure is referenced (Fig.24) but its numeric result is not in the exposed text.
project_relevance: Deltoris targets the compute and memory-traffic bottlenecks of diffusion-based VLA inference at the edge, relevant to AI accelerator architecture and HW/SW codesign. The bit-level temporal sparsity plus speculative-inference traffic amortization is a concrete mechanism for converting temporal redundancy into throughput. For the project card it is an accelerator/co-design study; the visible evidence does not establish production deployment or wafer-scale integration.
source_notes: arXiv preprint 2608.04428v1 (5 Aug 2026), FETCHED primary source; authors from SJTU, Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute, ICT CAS.
Headline 34.2x/6.1x speedups are abstract claims; per-baseline numeric breakdown is partly in unexposed result tables.
Baselines explicitly named: mobile Ampere GPU (Nvidia Orin), Pragmatic, BBS, Cambricon-D, Exion, Ditto.
